title: Change an engine air filter with the airbox cover held up on its duct, then clip shut
instruction: Change the engine air filter. The airbox's two clips are closed. Release both, hold the cover up out of the way, lift the old filter out and set it on its mat, put the new filter in its seat with its seal flat all round, lower the cover so its rear tabs go into the slots, and close both clips. Do not pull the cover off its intake duct or let a filter fall off the table.
context: Automotive service technicians and mechanics (SOC 49-3023, about 0.7 million US jobs, BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook), and the quick-lube technicians among them, inspect the engine air filter at nearly every oil change and scheduled service and replace it when dirty (about every 15,000 to 30,000 miles), so a busy shop changes several a day. The cover stays on the intake duct, which pulls it back toward its seat, so one hand holds it up and aside while the other takes out the old filter and drops the new one in. The pocket leaves the filter 6 mm of play; set down crooked or off, its edge rides up on the rim, its seal leaves a gap, and unfiltered air carrying dust goes past the filter into the engine. A rear tab that misses its slot leaves a gap at the back that leaks the same way, and a duct pulled hard tears or pops off the throttle body.
setup: Positions in metres (mm where stated) from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, z up from the table top; arm bases at (0, +0.305) and (0, -0.305). (1) Airbox lower case: one complete air cleaner assembly (case, cover, both clips) of a 2014 to 2019 Toyota Corolla 1.8 L, the one the FRAM CA10171 is listed for, its part number read off the case label and logged; nominal sizes as simulated (est; see Acceptance): 300 (x) by 240 (y) mm, centred x 360, y +10 mm, rim 75 mm up, on a steel stand (260 x 200 x 20 mm) fixed on rubber grommets. Its seat pocket is 252 x 185 mm and 30 mm deep (seat face 45 mm up). Two slots (12 x 26 mm, 17 mm deep) in the rear wall at y -60 and +80 mm. Two spring clips (the assembly's own) on the front wall at y -50 and +70 mm (0.12 m apart), simulated as steel rocker levers 12 mm wide, hinged on brackets (pivot x 145 mm, 96 mm up), thumb tab at x 105 mm, hook end at x 206 mm. Closed, the hook end lies 1 mm over the cover's catch lug. Pressing the thumb tab down past the middle (2 N, est) flips the clip released, its hook end 60 mm up; pushing the released lever's upper end back over the middle snaps it closed. (2) Cover: polypropylene, 300 x 240 x 40 mm, 3 mm walls, 0.28 kg (est), its rim on the case rim, roof 115 mm up. Two tabs (12 x 4 mm, 12 mm long) at y -60 and +80 mm, x 497 mm, sit in the slots (4 mm of play in x, 7 mm in y); a lift lug (an ABS block bonded on in the real build, where a mechanic's fingers take the cover), 20 mm (x 216 to 236) by 30 mm (y +5 to +35) and 20 mm tall, stands on the roof's front edge; two catch lugs (12 mm wide, 10 mm tall, 82 to 92 mm up) stick out 12 mm from the front wall at the clips. A 40 mm outlet at the rear (y +95 mm) joins a flexible intake duct to a fixed throttle-body stub (60 x 50 x 50 mm, x 590 to 650, y 70 to 120): 0.1 N per cm (est) on each axis, travel x +-40, y -40 to +300, up 80 mm. (3) Old filter in the seat and (4) new filter on the new-filter mat: FRAM CA10171 panel filters, est 240 x 173 x 49 mm, 0.15 kg, a 20 mm wide urethane frame, the pleat pack 26 mm tall (23 mm under the frame's top), a plain rectangle. Seated, the frame top is 94 mm up, 19 mm over the rim. The new one lies centred x 400, y -300 mm, turned a quarter turn: long side along y. Mats (2 mm): new-filter mat 200 x 250 mm there; old-filter mat 260 x 190 mm centred x 330, y -520. Engine-bay surroundings, fixed: a group 35 battery 230 x 175 x 225 mm centred x 645, y -260 (behind the right side of the box), and the radiator support's top edge, 20 mm x 0.9 m x 30 mm high, at x 90 to 110. Friction 0.6 filter to case, 0.5 elsewhere (est). Both grippers start open in their ready poses. Real build: the duct is a 300 mm length of flexible rubber hose sized to the outlet, clamped to it and looped back to a fixed stub at the stated place. Acceptance, before the first trial (luggage scale, rule): the filter seats flat in the pocket long side along x, either way round; held by its lift lug, the cover lifts 40 mm and moves 240 mm toward the stub for 1 to 4 N; each clip releases and closes for under 15 N; the seated filter's frame end takes a 20 mm pinch 13 mm deep clear of the case. An assembly that passes these checks is a valid build; its measured sizes replace the est ones.
scoring: End state, read at the last step from the poses of both filters, the cover, both clips and both grippers. Old out: the old filter's whole outline outside the case's footprint (x 210 to 510, y -110 to +130 mm) in top view, its lowest point within 6 mm of the table (a mat is 2 mm), tilted under 10 degrees. New seated: the new filter flat on the seat (all four bottom corners within 2 mm of the seat face, 45 mm up), its long side along the pocket, either way round (yaw within 5 degrees of 0 or 180), its centre within 6 mm of the pocket's, tilted under 3 degrees. Cover seated: rim within 2 mm of the case rim, both tabs in their slots (4 mm in x, 5 mm in y) at least 5 mm deep. Clipped: each clip's lever within 5 degrees of closed, resting on its lug, the cover seated. Hands off: on every step of the last 1 s both grippers' finger zones are 30 mm or more from the airbox, cover and both filters, and over that 1 s no filter moves 5 mm or turns 5 degrees, the cover moves under 5 mm and no clip turns 5 degrees. Score 0 if at any time the duct is overstretched (the cover more than 35 mm back or forward, 35 mm to the right of or 280 mm to the left of its seat, or 70 mm up: pulled off its stub) or a filter falls off the table (its lowest point more than 20 mm below the table top; lifting or carrying one is fine); and 0 unless hands off. A clip shut for a while on an empty box is no zero (the engine is off): the end state scores 0 unless the new filter is seated. Otherwise: 1.0 old out, new seated, cover seated, both clips clipped; 0.5 the same with a clip open; 0.25 old out and new seated, cover not seated; 0 otherwise. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. Success: 1.0 held for 1 s. In a real trial, per condition: old out by eye on a mat or the bench; new seated, after the trial with the cover lifted, a 2 mm feeler under the frame's corners and a rule from the pocket wall; cover seated, a 2 mm feeler round the rim and a torch at the rear slots; clipped, by eye and a light tug on the cover; hands off, a 30 mm spacer block and 30 fps video, nothing visibly moving; zero gates, the duct's travel marked with tape flags against a ruler, and the table edge by eye.
fidelity: Rigid bodies; shapes sized to the parts (est until measured; the real trial uses the real parts, checked as in setup's Acceptance); the pleat pack is rigid. The duct is not drawn: three springs of 0.1 N/cm (est); the cover only slides, it does not tilt. Clips are hinged levers with one declared rule: an over-centre spring to closed or released (2 N at the tab, est). Frictions 0.6 and 0.5 (est).
reset_notes: Close both clips over the cover's lugs with the cover down, its tabs in the slots. Put the old filter flat in the seat, long side along x. Lay the new filter on its mat at x 400, y -300 mm, long side along y. Clear the old-filter mat. Park both grippers open in their ready poses. Nothing is consumed.
